rows.question: In our compliance design, how does the retain-until-date differ between an object under variable retention with the event hold still on versus one whose hold was released, and can shortening the duration bring the date earlier in either case?

parts: How the retain-until-date behaves while the event hold is still on
How the retain-until-date behaves after the hold is released
Can shortening the duration bring the date earlier in either case

evidence.quote: While the event hold is on, Amazon S3 computes the retain-until-date as the current time plus the duration. The date moves forward as time passes.
When you release the event hold, Amazon S3 fixes the retain-until-date at the release time plus the duration, and the date stops changing.
If you decrease it, Amazon S3 does not set the retain-until-date to an earlier date than its current value.
When an object is locked in compliance mode, its retention mode can't be changed, and its retention period can't be shortened.

first.explanation: The 'Retain-until-date behavior with variable retention' section covers both states. While the hold is on, the date keeps moving forward, and shortening the duration never moves it earlier. On release, the date is fixed at release time plus duration. The page only describes changing the duration while the hold is on, and compliance mode says the retention period can't be shortened, so the answer is 'no' in both cases. Neither case says this in one sentence, so a strict grader could call the released case slightly implicit.

evidence.quote: While the event hold is on, Amazon S3 computes the retain-until-date as the current time plus the duration. The date moves forward as time passes.
If you decrease it, Amazon S3 does not set the retain-until-date to an earlier date than its current value.
When you release the event hold, Amazon S3 fixes the retain-until-date at the release time plus the duration, and the date stops changing.
When an object is locked in compliance mode, its retention mode can't be changed, and its retention period can't be shortened.

audit.explanation: The section 'Retain-until-date behavior with variable retention' covers both states. While the hold is on, the date moves forward and decreasing the duration never makes it earlier, with a worked example. On release, the date is fixed and stops changing. The Retention periods section also says the event hold duration can be changed only while the hold is on, and in compliance mode the retention period can't be shortened. So the answer for the released case is stated directly ('stops changing'), not inferred. This is the weakest of the 'full' items, but it holds.
